LESSON: SELF- ESTEEM ASSESSMENT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Population
Topic 1.2: Self- Esteem Assessment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Self- Esteem Assessment, part of People and Population in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is cultural heritage important to society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. a) The learner is guided to sign and fingerspell terms related to self –esteem b) Learners are guide in groups to use digital or print resources to search for and discuss the relationship between self-esteem and personal productivity. Guide learners to sit in horseshoe shape to enable them observe each other during the discussion. c) In pairs guide learners to refer to religious texts on self-love and share in class. d) Learners are guided in pairs to discuss cultural beliefs that promote self-esteem, e) In groups ,learners are guided to act out and discuss skits on examples of difficult life experiences that could severely affect self-esteem in their social lives, f) In groups ,learner is guided to discuss and present negative impact of low self-esteem such as: relationship difficulties, social isolation, g) In pairs, guide learners to discuss and share ways of seeking help to overcome low self-esteem and share the finding , The learners is guided to journalise actions they will take to improve their self-esteem.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. a) The learner is guided to sign and fingerspell terms related to self –esteem b) Learners are guide in groups to use digital or print resources to search for and discuss the relationship between self-esteem and personal productivity. Guide learners to sit in horseshoe shape to enable them observe each other during the discussion. c) In pairs guide learners to refer to religious texts on self-love and share in class. d) Learners are guided in pairs to discuss cultural beliefs that promote self-esteem, e) In groups ,learners are guided to act out and discuss skits on examples of difficult life experiences that could severely affect self-esteem in their social lives, f) In groups ,learner is guided to discuss and present negative impact of low self-esteem such as: relationship difficulties, social isolation, g) In pairs, guide learners to discuss and share ways of seeking help to overcome low self-esteem and share the finding , The learners is guided to journalise actions they will take to improve their self-esteem.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Self- Esteem Assessment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: learners develop speaking skills as they discuss cultural beliefs that promote self- esteem.

Digital literacy: learners use digital devices to search for the relationship between self-esteem and personal productivity

Values:
• -love: learners honestly journalise on steps they would take to improve their self-esteem.

Responsibility: learners commit themselves through journalising actions they will take to improve their self-esteem.

Link to Other Subjects:

• Religious Education: learners discuss about self-love from religious texts.

Kenyan Sign Language, Kiswahili and English: learners make journal entries on steps they would take to improve their self-esteem.

Suggested Learning Resources:

artifacts, museums, library resources, approved textbooks, digital devices, ,maps, resource person,

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Guidance and peer counselling: learners discuss and share ways of seeking help to overcome low self-esteem.

Social cohesion: learners work together in groups to discuss cultural beliefs that promote self-esteem.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: Why is cultural heritage important to society?
